name: Arcus Perps BridgeVault

requirements.label: Admin power is not a bare key
A confirmed delay before changes apply, no bypass
Bypass paths of the delay checked and ruled out
Price feed not under one hand
No key shared with another tracked protocol

exit_window: none: a change applies at once

narrative.summary: Deposit and withdrawal custody vault for Arcus Perps. Its admin role is held by a real 24-hour timelock and, in parallel, by a validator contract whose 2-of-3 bare-EOA quorum can, per Arcus’s published ABI, run arbitrary calls with only a deadline field, so the delay may not bind that path.
narrative.detail: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by three contracts: the timelock (getMinDelay 86,400s), ValidatorConsensus (threshold 2 of 3 validators, all bare EOAs) and CheckpointManager. The timelock’s proposer, executor and canceller roles are held by ValidatorConsensus, CheckpointManager and one further address, a 2-of-4 Safe that is also one of the three owners of the Arcus pToken 2-of-3 Safe, which is why crossExposureScore is 80. Arcus publishes ABIs only, so the claim that the validator quorum can route around the delay comes from the signature of executeGovernanceAction (arbitrary calls plus a deadline, no delay field), not from source, and that function has never run (executedGovernanceCount is 0).

steps.what: getRoleMember(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0) on the contract (AccessControl, enumerable): the holder
getMinDelay() on the holder (OpenZeppelin TimelockController), in seconds
the implementation slot of the proxy (EIP-1967): the code behind it, an upgrade changes this word
